settings.definition_quote: In the fixed-confidence setting a maximal risk $\delta$ is fixed, and one looks for a strategy guaranteeing that $\bP(\hat{a}_\tau\notin\text{argmax}\, \mu_a) \leq \delta$ (such a strategy is called $\delta$-PAC) while minimizing the sample complexity $\bE[\tau]$.

source.label: cor:GeneBAI
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1)$. For any $\delta$-PAC strategy and any bandit model $\bm\mu\in\cS$, \[\bE_{\bm \mu}[\tau_\delta] \geq T^*(\bm\mu)\,\kl(\delta,1-\delta), \] where $T^*(\bm \mu)^{-1} := \sup_{w \in \Sigma_K} \inf_{\bm \lambda \in \Alt(\bm\mu)} ( \sum_{a=1}^K w_a d(\mu_a,\lambda_a))$.

results.notes: Algorithm class: delta-PAC strategies. Remark 2.2 gives the asymptotic consequence liminf E[tau]/log(1/delta) >= T*(mu), and the non-asymptotic kl(delta,1-delta) >= log(1/(2.4 delta)).

source.label: prop:deltaPAC
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1)$. Whatever the sampling strategy, using Chernoff's stopping rule~\eqref{def:Stopping} on Bernoulli bandits with threshold \[\beta(t,\delta) = \log \left(\frac{2t (K-1)}{\delta}\right)\] ensures that for all $\bm\mu \in \cS$, $\bP_{\bm\mu}\left(\tau_\delta<\infty, \,\hat{a}_{\tau_\delta} \neq a^*\right) \leq \delta.$

results.notes: delta-PAC guarantee (error probability <= delta), holds for every instance. Mapping of probability field is approximate.

tuning: beta(t,delta) = log(C t^alpha / delta) with alpha > 1 and a constant C = C(alpha, K) whose existence is shown

source.label: prop:PACGene
source.quote: Let $\bm \mu$ be an exponential family bandit model. Let $\delta \in (0,1)$ and $\alpha>1$. There exists a constant $C=C(\alpha,K)$ such that whatever the sampling strategy, using Chernoff's stopping rule~\eqref{def:Stopping} with the threshold \[\beta(t,\delta)=\log \left(\frac{C t^\alpha}{\delta}\right)\] ensures that for all $\bm\mu \in \cS$, $\bP_{\bm\mu}\big(\tau_\delta<\infty, \, \hat{a}_{\tau_\delta} \neq a^*\big) \leq \delta.$

results.notes: delta-PAC guarantee for general one-parameter exponential families.

symbols.alpha_thr: exponent alpha in [1, e/2] of the threshold r(t)=O(t^alpha)

tuning: beta(t,delta) = log(r(t)/delta) with r(t) = O(t^alpha_thr), alpha_thr in [1, e/2]
any sampling rule with N_a(t)/t -> w*_a almost surely (e.g. C-Tracking or D-Tracking)

source.label: lem:AnalysisAS
source.quote: Let $\alpha\in [1,e/2]$ and $r(t) = O(t^\alpha)$. Using Chernoff's stopping rule with $\beta(t,\delta)=\log(r(t)/\delta)$, and any sampling rule ensuring that for every arm $a\in\Arms$, $N_a(t)/t$ converges almost-surely to $w_a^*$ guarantees that for all $\delta\in (0,1)$, $\bP_{\bm\mu}(\tau_\delta < +\infty)=1$ and \[\bP_{\bm\mu}\left(\limsup_{\delta \rightarrow 0}\frac{\tau_\delta}{\log(1/\delta)} \leq \alpha T^*(\bm \mu) \right) = 1.\]

results.notes: Applies to any sampling rule with converging proportions; C/D-Tracking satisfy this by Proposition 3.3. Also states tau_delta finite a.s.

symbols.alpha_thr: exponent alpha in [1, e/2] of the threshold r(t)=O(t^alpha)

tuning: beta(t,delta) = log(r(t)/delta) with r(t) = O(t^alpha_thr), alpha_thr in [1, e/2]

source.label: thm:AsymptoticSC
source.quote: Let $\bm\mu$ be an exponential family bandit model. Let $\alpha\in [1,e/2]$ and $r(t) = O(t^\alpha)$. Using Chernoff's stopping rule with $\beta(t,\delta)=\log(r(t)/\delta)$, and the sampling rule C-Tracking or D-Tracking, \[\limsup_{\delta \rightarrow 0} \frac{\bE_{\bm\mu}[\tau_\delta]}{\log(1/\delta)} \leq {\alpha}{T^*(\bm\mu)}\;.\]

results.notes: Combined with Theorem 4.1 (Bernoulli, alpha=1 threshold log(2(K-1)t/delta)) gives asymptotic optimality, matching Theorem 2.1.
